content: The provided text appears to be a list of references from scientific literature, primarily focused on studies and evaluations related to hepatitis C virus (HCV) core antigen detection methods, their diagnostic utility, and their comparison with other diagnostic techniques such as HCV RNA assays. 1. Gu SJ, Liu J, Zhang HJ, Gu BL, Lai HJ, Zhou HL, et al. conducted a meta-analysis on core antigen tests for hepatitis C virus (HCV), published in Molecular Biology Reports in 2012. The study evaluated the diagnostic performance of these tests in detecting HCV infection. 2. Hadziyannis E, Vassilopoulos D, Georgiou A, Spanou F, Koskinas J. compared a novel automated immunoassay for HCV core antigen detection with quantitative HCV RNA measurement in patients with chronic hepatitis C. This study was presented in Hepatology in 2010. 3. Hayashi K, Hasuike S, Kusumoto K, Ido A, Uto H, Kenji N, et al. assessed the utility of a new immunoradiometric assay for detecting HCV core antigen in a community-based population. Their findings were published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2005. 4. Heidrich B, Pischke S, Kirschner J, Schneider J, Mederacke I, Raupach R, et al. evaluated the performance of HCV core antigen testing in liver transplant recipients. This study was presented in the Journal of Hepatology in 2011. 5. Higashimoto M, Takahashi M, Jokyu R, Syundou H, Saito H. improved the sensitivity of the second-generation HCV core antigen assay using a novel concentration method involving polyethylene glycol (PEG). Their work was published in Rinsho Byori in 2007. 6. Hmaïed F, Ben Mamou M, Arrouji Z, Slim A, Ben Redjeb S. explored the combined detection of HCV core antigen and antibodies to reduce the serological window phase. This study was published in Pathologie Biologie (Paris) in 2007. 7. Hosseini-Moghaddam SM, Iran-Pour E, Rotstein C, Husain S, Lilly L, Renner E, et al. reviewed the clinical applicability of HCV core antigen testing, discussing its potential advantages and limitations for diagnosis and follow-up. This review appeared in Reviews in Medical Virology in 2012. 8. Icardi G, Ansaldi F, Bruzzone BM, Durando P, Lee S, de Luigi C, et al. clinically evaluated a novel enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for HCV core antigen detection, aiming to reduce the HCV window period. Their findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2001. 9. Icardi G, Bruzzone B, Gota F, Torre F, Giannini E, Massone L, et al. developed a new assay for HCV core antigen detection as an alternative to nucleic acid technologies in anti-HCV-positive or indeterminate subjects. This study was published in Annals of Igiene in 2003. 10. Irshad M, Dhar I, Joshi YK. investigated the significance of HCV core protein in diagnosing HCV infection across various liver diseases. Their findings were published in the Journal of Investigative Medicine in 2006. 11. Irshad M, Dhar I, Khushboo, Singh S, Kapoor S. compared serological and nucleic acid-based assays for diagnosing HCV infection in acute and chronic liver diseases. This study was published in the International Journal of Health Sciences (Qassim) in 2007. 12. Ivanov YD, Kaysheva AL, Frantsuzov PA, Pleshakova TO, Krohin NV, Izotov AA, et al. utilized atomic force microscopy combined with mass spectrometry to detect HCV core protein in serum. Their work was published in the International Journal of Nanomedicine in 2015. 13. Ivanyi-Nagy R, Makowska Z, Lastra ML, Darlix JL. provided an overview of the properties and functions of the HCV core protein in a textbook chapter published by Nova Science Publishers in 2010. 14. Kamili S, Drobeniuc J, Araujo AC, Hayden TM. reviewed laboratory diagnostics for HCV infection, highlighting the role of core antigen assays. This review appeared in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2012. 15. Kashiwakuma T, Hasegawa A, Kajita T, Takata A, Mori H, Ohta Y, et al. developed a sensitive fluorescence enzyme immunoassay (FEIA) for detecting HCV-specific core protein in serum. Their findings were published in the Journal of Immunological Methods in 1996. 16. Kenfe FR, Urbaczek AC, Silva JC, Neó TA, Da Silva FH, Da Costa PI. studied the immunoreactivity of recombinant HCV core and E2 proteins fused to GST with control serum positive for HCV. Their work was published in Talanta in 2013. 17. Kesli R, Polat H, Terzi Y, Kurtoglu MG, Uyar Y. compared a newly developed automated and quantitative HCV core antigen test with HCV RNA assays for confirming anti-HCV results. This study was published in Clinical Microbiology and Infection in 2012. 18. Kocazeybek B, Yuksel P, Saribas S, Caliskan R, Ergin S, Aslan M, et al. evaluated the diagnostic performance of a new HCV core antigen detection test in in-vitro diagnosis of HCV infections. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2010. 19. Krajden M, Shivji R, Gunadasa K, Mak A, McNabb G, Friesenhahn M, et al. assessed the core antigen assay as a second-line supplemental test for diagnosing active HCV infection. This study was published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2004. 20. Kuo YH, Lu SN. questioned whether HCV core antigen is an adequate marker for community screening. Their findings were presented in Hepatology International in 2012.
